instruction: I need to count my total finance documents. Please create a text file at /home/user/Documents/pdf_count.txt containing the total number of PDF files in the /home/user/Documents/Finance/receipts/ directory.

metadata.explanation: Task requires counting PDF files in receipts directory. Config downloads 6 PDF files: 5 AWS invoices (2308-2312) plus 1 X-receipt. Evaluator checks if created file contains '6'.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both instruction requirements: (1) file exists at /home/user/Documents/pdf_count.txt (vm_file getter fails if missing) and (2) file contains correct count (metric compares to 6)

Metric function correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': directly accesses expected.get('expected_number') at line 19, does NOT incorrectly use expected.get('rules', {}) or expected.get('type'). This follows framework requirements from guidance section 5.1

Data flow is semantically correct: vm_file getter fetches file content as bytes (file.py:110-126) -> passes bytes to metric as 'result' parameter -> metric decodes bytes to string with result.decode('utf-8').strip() at line 24 -> parses as integer at line 28 -> compares to expected_number (6) at line 29

Expected value is semantically correct: config downloads exactly 6 PDF files to /home/user/Documents/Finance/receipts/ (aws-invoice-2308.pdf, 2309.pdf, 2310.pdf, 2311.pdf, 2312.pdf, X-receipt-2312.pdf). Expected value of 6 matches actual PDF count
Complete instruction coverage: evaluator verifies file creation (implicit - vm_file getter fails if file doesn't exist) and correct numeric content (explicit - metric checks content == 6)
Robust edge case handling: metric catches ValueError for non-integer content (lines 33-35), decode errors and other exceptions (lines 37-40), returning 0.0 for all failure cases
No state timing issues: file will persist after task completion, no UI dependencies, no postconfig needed

Static warnings are false positives: metric DOES consume vm_file result correctly. The vm_file getter returns file content as bytes (not a file path), which the metric correctly decodes at line 24. Static analyzer incorrectly expects path operations, but vm_file returns content directly

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_numeric_content__66b5cf7b first parameter type (bytes) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
